summary: Recent discussions in the Parquet community focus on clarifying how FILE logical types with both inline data and a URI should be interpreted, revisiting the 8 KB page size recommendation, and extending the OffsetIndex to expose page sizes for better memory management. A proposal to introduce a SERIALIZED_VALUE logical type for BYTE_ARRAY columns that store protobuf, FlatBuffers, or Thrift messages is also underway. These threads illustrate ongoing efforts to improve data representation, performance, and interoperability.

highlights.text: Clarification needed on how a FILE logical type with both inline data and a URI locator should be interpreted, as different readers may return different bytes.

sources.title: [DISCUSS] Ambiguity in the FILE logical type when inline and uri are both set

highlights.text: Discussion to remove the 8 KB page size recommendation in the Parquet documentation, citing that 8 KB is too small for compression.
Proposal to add uncompressed page size and dictionary page size to the Parquet OffsetIndex so readers can bound memory usage before fetching pages.

sources.title: [DISCUSS] Page sizes in the OffsetIndex, to let readers bound memory up front

highlights.text: Proposal to introduce a SERIALIZED_VALUE logical type for BYTE_ARRAY columns that store serialized protobuf, FlatBuffers, or Thrift messages, recording the message format.
